clue.text: The strength of the corporation head

parts.note: a corporation is a business, a firm
a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: A remark on how strong the company's chief executive is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the boss of the corporation, but it is a geographical head: NESS, a promontory, common in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmness is solidity and resolve, a kind of strength.

clue.text: Frustrated at being given food containing oil

indicators.note: containing means the word for fed goes round the other piece

parts.note: given food means fed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed to be served an oily meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Foiled means thwarted, so a foiled plan leaves its maker frustrated.

clue.text: Fires possibly about fifty guns

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
possibly suggests the letters of fires could be arranged differently

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Around fifty weapons may be discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges FIRES to RIFES, and 'about' wraps that round the L for fifty, a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Rifles are long-barrelled firearms, a kind of gun.

clue.text: A girl left behind — as usual!

indicators.note: behind means the letter for left comes after the name

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a girl was abandoned once again, as always.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means ordinary, what is typical or customary.

clue.text: The main boy-friend at a particular time

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a son is a boy
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A girl's boyfriend works at sea, home only part of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the poetic name for the ocean; 'boy-friend' splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonally means according to the seasons, happening at certain times of year.

clue.text: A bouquet for the climber

definitions.note: the definition names the person; the answer is the upward journey the climber makes

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its aroma, its scent

explanation.surface: Someone presents a bunch of flowers to a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, but here it is a smell. The definition is loose: the answer is the climb the climber undertakes, not the climber.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber's purpose is to go up, and a rise up a slope is what the climber attempts.

clue.text: Produce notes about sound use of 2

indicators.note: about means the word for producing notes goes round the other piece

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes
a hoot is a sound, as an owl or horn makes

explanation.surface: A remark about making music and the acoustic use of firearms.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' refers to the answer at 2 down, RIFLES; firing rifles is this activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing guns is the act of discharging them, the activity rifles serve.

clue.text: Appeal for tea perhaps sitting in a doorway

indicators.note: sitting in means the rearranged letters are placed inside the doorway word

parts.note: an entry is a doorway or entrance

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of tea may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sits in a doorway begging for a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a beggar in a doorway; in fact 'perhaps' rearranges the drink into EAT, and 'sitting in' seats that inside the doorway word.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request, a plea or appeal.

clue.text: The small all round charge for birds

indicators.note: all round means the first pieces go around the other word

parts.note: to charge is to rush forward

explanation.surface: A modest fee is levied on everything to feed birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrushes are songbirds such as the blackbird and song thrush.

clue.text: Modish plant almost everyone finds odious

parts.note: something modish is fashionable, or in
a fern is a leafy green plant

indicators.note: almost means the word for everyone loses its final letter

parts.note: everyone is all

explanation.surface: Everybody seems to dislike a trendy houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal literally means hellish, and colloquially detestable or odious.

clue.text: A person well able to deal with any ill feeling!

definitions.text: A person well able to deal with any ill feeling!

parts.words: A person well able to deal with any ill feeling
parts.note: ill feeling reads as resentment, but literally it is feeling unwell, which a medical professional treats

explanation.surface: Praise for someone skilled at smoothing over grudges and hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: A physician treats patients who feel sick, so they deal with feeling ill.

clue.text: Tea-lover maybe, getting a lift from it

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the hyphenated word could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A tea drinker gets a pick-me-up from a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lift' looks like a pick-me-up from tea; it is the American word for a lift between floors.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevator is the American name for a lift carrying people between floors of a building.

clue.text: Downright second gives voice

parts.note: downright, as in utter nonsense, means complete or utter

explanation.surface: A blunt follow-up remark is spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to speak it, to give voice to it.

clue.text: The youngest students are quite outstanding

definitions.meaning: in a school the lowest year group, the starting class, holds the youngest pupils

explanation.definitionFit: The first class of a school is its youngest pupils, and first-rate quality is the highest.

clue.text: Figure there must be strings attached

definitions.text: Figure there must be strings attached

parts.words: Figure there must be strings attached
parts.note: strings attached reads as hidden conditions on a deal, but literally a puppet figure hangs from strings

explanation.surface: Someone suspects that a generous offer comes with hidden conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet worked by strings is a figure with strings literally attached.

clue.text: Detain the rogue? No sir, on reflection

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rogue

indicators.note: on reflection means the words no sir are mirrored, read backwards

explanation.surface: A villain is to be held, though he protests, and the officer reconsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprison someone is to lock them up, to detain them.

clue.text: Accommodation for workers — a self-build project

definitions.text: Accommodation for workers — a self-build project

parts.words: Accommodation for workers — a self-build project
parts.note: workers suggests a staff hostel, but the worker caste of a colony builds its own home

explanation.surface: Housing for employees that they must construct themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker insects construct their own colony home from soil and debris.

clue.text: Avoiding all duty is his aim in life

definitions.text: Avoiding all duty is his aim in life

parts.words: Avoiding all duty is his aim in life
parts.note: duty reads as obligation, but in the customs sense it is the tax on imported goods that a contraband runner evades

explanation.surface: A portrait of a shirker whose ambition is to dodge responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone running contraband avoids paying customs taxes on goods.

clue.text: A Menshevik of note — a heel

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
to heel is to lean over, as a ship does, which is to list

explanation.surface: A notable Russian revolutionary is denounced as a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mensheviks, the minority faction of Russian socialists, were called minimalists in English because they sought minimum reforms. 'Heel' looks like a cad but is the sailing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimalist was the English name given to a Menshevik, a moderate of the Russian revolutionary movement.

clue.text: Big safety device

definitions.meaning: very large, as in a ... crop
a car's buffer that absorbs impact

explanation.definitionFit: A bumper harvest is a huge one, and a car's front and rear guard is a protective fitting.

clue.text: Not in a bad state

indicators.note: bad signals the letters of not in a are in a poor, disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone says they are feeling fine, not in poor condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A state in the political sense is a country, a nation.

clue.text: Try climbing in a tree raised as a bush!

indicators.note: in means one reversed word is placed inside the other
in a down clue raised means the tree word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an elm is a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means try is read bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: An attempt to climb a tree that turns out to be only a shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' and 'raised' both read upwards, giving YRT and MLE; 'in' then nests the first inside the second. The surface's tree-versus-bush contrast is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Singer made to give up

indicators.note: made here means forced into a new form, so the letters of singer are reworked

explanation.surface: A vocalist is forced to abandon a career.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to quit a post, to give it up.

clue.text: Article about clerical employment showing soundness

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
C stands for circa, Latin for about
a curacy is the post of a curate, a junior clergyman

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concerns jobs in the church and their good standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness of a reading or argument is its correctness, its exactness.

clue.text: Getting fish into a pen can be very hard

indicators.note: getting into means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
an eel is a long snakelike fish

explanation.surface: Getting a fish into a pen is a tough job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steely is like steel: unyielding and very hard.

clue.text: Bias is not commonly an indication of militancy

parts.note: a warp is a twist or bias in judgment
ain't is the colloquial form of is not

explanation.surface: A remark that prejudice is not usually a sign of aggression.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors paint their faces before battle, so face paint signals readiness to fight.

clue.text: It's no thanks to the railway official!

parts.note: taken as written
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A passenger snubs a railway employee with a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a public officer who certifies documents, an official.

clue.text: Split using reagents

indicators.note: using signals that the letters of reagents are employed to make a new word

explanation.surface: A chemist separates a mixture with laboratory chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to drive them apart, to split them up.
